`financial-lifecycle-compact-lower.ts` and `lowerFinancialLifecycleCompact` are proposed, absent interfaces. Before behavioral edits, freeze their exact signature and output and the consuming versioned artifact schema. Compile input is the primitive source and exact profile/bounds/lowering identity; output binds the source-derived schema, ordered Core/actions, generated Compact and complete state/argument/effect mapping. Runtime PRE comes from the authenticated native predecessor. A host-funded result, validity boolean or post-state callback is never authority.

Generation must implement all operations, dynamic arguments and assertions used by the reviewed lifecycle source. Source constants may be compiled as constants; expected outputs cannot replace source semantics. Unsupported lowering must reject explicitly and remain an open wider-language obligation. Preserve all existing Source5 bounds, prior profiles, fixed recovery paths, wallet identities, keys and deployments.

## Required identity and acceptance contract

**program-and-artifacts — LL04.1 / original 5.1; 5.1a.** Bind exact primitive source bytes and hash, source/5, expression Core/4, lifecycle kernel/state versions, complete source-derived schema and ordered action Core, selected action, registered bounds/canonicalization, lowering version, generated Compact, actual compiler/ZKIR/runtime/key artifact identities. Source review freezes this map; LL06 supplies real compiler evidence. Dynamic arguments remain constrained by the generated source program. Enforcement: Source elaboration -> lifecycle lowerer -> generator -> build source manifest -> executable asset loader -> actual SDK call.

**deployment-and-head — LL04.1; lifecycle-ledger-integration/Authenticated financial state and actual language consumer.** Bind network identity/genesis and expected protocol, contract/deployment and instance, immutable program/profile, accepted head and revision, ordinary PRE plus complete lifecycle PRE. Expected revision must be read from and consumed against actual state; constrain read-then-write, reject stale conflict, no blind overwrite or arbitrary JSON state. Enforcement: Generator/circuits, integration preflight, native observer; full theorem/deploy audit remains SP09.

**auth-and-consent — LL04.1/LL04.4; loan-origination-accrual/Explicit funded origination and authority boundary.** Originate proves lender funding authority AND debtor consent for exact obligation/roles/terms/cap/program/head. Transfer consumes matching native funded source once. Repay/settle require actual borrower funding authority for selected amount and recipient; lender receipt is no spending authority. Accrue requires the reviewed action permission and previously consented terms/time/cap; choice of principal permission is frozen before implementation. A role secret, local allowance or maintenance signing key alone is not debtor consent. Enforcement: Circuit authority envelope plus existing wallet/UTXO enforcement; exact action-permission design review pending.

**state-completeness — LL04.5; bounded-loan-lifecycle/Complete conservation observation.** Persist every field of the listed LifecycleState and ordinary post state, including unrelated rows, complete obligation birth terms and cumulative counters, all four ordered ID lists, and full history interpretation. No state normalization may drop fields, sort semantic arrays, delete settled obligations, erase identities or refund work. Retain ordered full effects per accepted action and authenticate their linkage through ledger transition history; the exact physical history encoding must be frozen before implementation. Enforcement: Generated state/circuit update plus complete decoder and comparator.

**bounds-and-staging — LL04.3–LL04.6; all four financial-postconditions requirements.** Preserve closed schemas and canonical numeric distinctions, U128/signed128/U64 ranges, checked intermediate arithmetic, 128 collection capacities and 65536-byte lifecycle state limits. Check all actions including unselected/dead branches; prefix once, kernel once, suffix once. PRE stays immutable, ordinary POST staged, six financial POST reads inspect actual tentative kernel state. Reject without financial/post/effects/identity publication; source, kernel and ensure error precedence stays scoped and observable. Enforcement: Actual source/compiler and generated transition; independent offline and compiled runtime controls.

**work — LL04.5; financial-postconditions/Exact staged work and error precedence.** Carry remaining/spent/closureReserve and workInitial equality across all actions. Debit actual prefix+kernel+suffix only on accepted state; rejected attempt evidence may report attempted work but may not consume predecessor success state. No reset across serialization/continuation or reserve spending. Enforcement: Generated fields, constraints, decoder and complete oracle.

**time — LL04.1/LL04.3; loan-origination-accrual/Monotone period and duplicate protection.** Accrue observedTime is the same UInt64 value constrained by blockTimeGte and blockTimeLt(value+300), with overflow/horizon checks; also observedTime>=nextAccrualAt and periodIndex=last+1. Do not infer time from an unconstrained host read. Existing source firstPeriodStart1000 is unchanged; actual observation T may be current ledger time, not the local demo1060. Tests replace whole QueryContext.block including uncertainty and read it back. Enforcement: Reuse reviewed constrainNow semantics in new generated lifecycle, actual caller and compiled runtime tests.

**native-effects-and-fees — LL04.1/LL04.6; lifecycle-ledger-integration/Docker financial lifecycle before Preview.** Cash denomination/asset maps to exact native token color/domain/issuing contract and role addresses; prove gross funding, recipients, net credits, change and custody reserve deltas for each transfer. Record every native input/output/transcript and enforce original caps on gross input debit, not refunded/net values. Financial allowance spent100/110 is distinct from gross UTXO input totals with change. DUST vFee/SPECK is measured separately and cumulatively against admitted cap; no old slack reuse. Extra assets/calls/recipients or mismatched payer reject. Enforcement: Generated receive/send effects, native signed offers, provider reservations, observer/comparator.

**initialization — LL04.4/LL04.5; original 5.1a.** Initialization must authenticate source-independent initial context against real native balances/setup effects: lenderCash100, borrowerCash10 and unchanged Other/Token row, no obligation, exact allowances/work/ordinary PRE. Any authorized test-asset mint/funding setup is a separately named actual setup effect bound to recipients and source/profile. It cannot masquerade as lender disbursement or confer new liability consent; old borrower20-billion mint is not Source5 initialization. Enforcement: Reviewed constructor/setup path, authentic readback and later originate.

**consumer-and-evidence — LL04.4/LL04.7; original 5.3; LL06–LL08.** Real SDK caller selects generated action and arguments from checked source and authenticated predecessor, retains source/artifact identities before every call, and compares full actual outputs independently. Adapters and host flags remain source-test-only. Compiler success, raw main exit, containment, Docker result and finalized Preview acceptance remain distinct later gates. No public argv/allocation or transaction count is invented here. Enforcement: Actual integrateLocalFinancialCase/runFinancialCase/proven-assets/provider/observer consumers.

## Complete expected lifecycle

This is independent financial arithmetic derived from the checked source terms and supplied starting context, not an execution result. Initialize the authenticated ordinary state `phase=0, paid=0`; financial balances are lender Cash100, borrower Cash10 and Other Token7. Allowances are lender remaining100/spent0, borrower110/0 and Other Token3/1. Obligations and all four identity histories start empty; work starts remaining512/spent17/reserve16. Initialization funding/mint provenance and permissions need actual reviewed setup evidence.

| Source action | Principal/accrued/outstanding | Lender/borrower Cash | Borrower allowance remaining/spent | phase/paid | Work remaining/spent/reserve |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| originate | 100/0/100 | 0/110 | 110/0 | 1/0 | 413/116/16 |
| accrue | 100/10/110 | 0/110 | 110/0 | 2/0 | 348/181/16 |
| repay | 80/0/80 | 30/80 | 80/30 | 3/30 | 260/269/16 |
| settle | 0/0/0 | 110/0 | 0/110 | 4/110 | 174/355/16 |

Originate emits ordered `Transfer D1` then `Origination O1` for Loan1. Accrue emits `Accrual A1`; period advances0→1 and next eligibility1060→1120. Repay30 emits `Transfer P1` then `Repayment R1`, discharging interest10 and principal20. Settle computes outstanding80 in source, then emits `Transfer P2` and `Repayment R2`, discharging principal80. All seven full effect records are in the JSON; no metadata or order may be dropped.

Loan1 retains debtor, creditor, denomination, settlement asset, conversion1/scale0/rounding none, AccrualFirst allocation, initialPrincipal100, cap110, origin/funding IDs, rate1/10 floor, period60 and firstPeriodStart1000. Lifetime incurred becomes110 and remains110 at settlement. The settled obligation remains present. Lender allowance remains0/100 after origination. Other Token7 and allowance3/1 never change. Transfer history becomes `[D1,P1,P2]`, allocation history `[R1,R2]`, origination history `[O1]` and accrual history `[A1]`; these remain ordered and present.

The live accrual time is symbolic `T`: the actual UInt64 observation used by both source Accrue and the block-time constraint. The local demo1060 is not a live timestamp. A current T≥1060 is permitted by the existing source; no edit to its firstPeriodStart is inferred. Full effects record T. Work costs99/65/88/86 are inherited reviewed source references; independent AST reduction validation remains required for the frozen generated candidate.

Native transfers are lender→borrower100, no cash movement for accrual, borrower→lender30, then borrower→lender80. Financial allowance spent measures those authorized transfers. Gross native UTXO inputs may be larger because of change and must satisfy separate gross caps; measured DUST fees have their own cumulative SPECK cap. Never invent fee amounts or approve new resources from this arithmetic.

## Independent rejection cases

Each case below is specified-only and retains its constraint-to-original-requirement mapping in the JSON. Exercise relevant cases through the actual caller and generated runtime after source review; injected transport remains offline evidence.

| Case | Mutation | Required observation |
|---|---|---|
| LL04-N01 | Replace source bytes/action order/schema/Core while keeping old program/artifact hash. | Reject before signing/submission; never run old atomic artifact. |
| LL04-N02 | Correct source hash with old initialize/accrue/settle generated module or substituted verifier/ZKIR. | Asset loader/caller rejects. |
| LL04-N03 | Use right source/state on wrong network genesis, deployment, contract instance, head or revision; replay one head in two valid-looking calls. | Reject mismatched context; both conflicts cannot consume same head. |
| LL04-N04 | Raise cap110 to120 and incurred counter consistently in supplied financial PRE while preserving superficial state invariants. | Authenticated state/consent rejection even if local state admission succeeds. |
| LL04-N05 | Originate with lender capability only, debtor capability only, wrong terms/cap/role consent, or reused consent against another program/head. | Reject missing or substituted authority; no debt/movement. |
| LL04-N06 | Originate100 using borrower/third-party UTXOs, wrong asset/recipient, absent Transfer or previously consumed D1 funding. | Reject actual funding mismatch; no obligations, balances, allowances or successful IDs change. |
| LL04-N07 | Use lender receiving capability as permission to debit borrower on repay/settle; swap addresses or payer binding between stages. | Reject; no blanket lender settlement authority or unnoticed provider replacement. |
| LL04-N08 | Set observedTime1060 while replace whole block context with time1059; or use block>=observedTime+300, overlarge UInt64 window, wrong horizon; change only one of eligibility/circuit time arguments. | Generated acceptance rejects with real context constraints; whole-context readback demonstrates mutation took effect. |
| LL04-N09 | After period1 and repay, repeat A1 or period1; use fresh ID with skipped/reversed period or observedTime1059. | Reject with unchanged predecessor state; no period/work/history reset. |
| LL04-N10 | At outstanding80 change principal80/accrued0 to70/10 so aggregate stays80; erase initialPrincipal/incurred/cap/cursor or settled obligation. | Complete decoder/comparator and authenticated transition reject. |
| LL04-N11 | Keep borrower remaining allowance80 but forge spent0; replace Other/Token amount7 or allowance3/1; reorder/drop arrays or history IDs. | Reject complete state mismatch; unrelated rows survive byte-faithful semantic projection. |
| LL04-N12 | Replay transfer/allocation/origination/accrual ID within its namespace, reset history on serialization, or consume one funding record twice. | Reject duplicate/consumption violation. Equal spelling across distinct permitted namespaces is not falsely rejected. |
| LL04-N13 | Set workInitial to prior512 during continuation; reset spent17, borrow closure reserve, or provide one fewer exact spendable unit. | Reject atomically; exact cost boundary succeeds with reserve unchanged. |
| LL04-N14 | After repay kernel, change ensure outstanding80 to79 in a separately identified source variant; inject financial POST via snapshot or callback. | Type/source interface or actual suffix rejects; no native transfer can publish before ensure success. |
| LL04-N15 | Ill-typed unselected action/dead-branch financial POST; use post read outside ensures, ordinary next to debt or period cursor. | Static rejection before ledger caller and no financial mutation. |
| LL04-N16 | Zero denominator, negative nominal, U128 multiplication overflow, signed nominal overflow, U64 time overflow, overcapacity or oversized state; truncate to fit. | Bounded typed rejection, no wrap/truncation or silently smaller accepted language. |
| LL04-N17 | Change ordered effects, transfer metadata or equal-total principal/interest split while preserving final balance/debt. | Comparator rejects each changed field and order. |
| LL04-N18 | Input gross150, lender receipt100, change50 under gross cap100; or add fee/recipient/asset/call and compensate net total elsewhere. | Gross cap and complete native-effect checks reject; refunds cannot conceal spend. |
| LL04-N19 | Forge indexer fee label with native DUST vFee unchanged; exceed cumulative current allocation or reuse historical unused capacity. | Native SPECK comparison/resource boundary rejects; no tolerance or old-slack transfer. |
| LL04-N20 | Provide right JSON financialPost with missing/mismatched native movement, indexer-only inclusion or noncanonical finalized block. | No financial acceptance; incomplete evidence remains incomplete. |
| LL04-N21 | Legacy caller reports FINANCIAL_COMPLETE after four stages without originate/repay, or omits failed action native before/after capture. | Lifecycle result remains incomplete regardless of wrapper status. |
| LL04-N22 | Compute source repay nominal29 (or31) after accrued110, or settle a zero-debt state; fake host prepared flag. | Source ensures / positive-payment guard reject; independent input-dependent circuit behavior must agree. |

## Decisions that must be frozen before implementation

1. Exact action authority: lender funding plus debtor consent at origination, explicit accrue permission, borrower funding authority at repayment/settlement, all bound to terms/cap/program/head. The existing two constructor secrets and maintenance signing key do not establish that contract by themselves. No blanket lender settlement authority is inferred.
2. Exact full state/history encoding and decoder, preserving every field, bound, ordered identity namespace and complete effects. A compiler limit cannot silently omit fields or shrink the accepted language. Use the existing ledger history; add no generic history framework.
3. Actual existing lender funding path and borrower continuation path, native asset identity and initialization reserve provenance. The current single borrower payer and fixed20-billion borrower mint fail this predicate.
4. Exact source-derived lowerer outputs and versioned generator/build/loader/SDK/comparator consumers. The current fixed recovery plan must remain historical. `run-local.mjs`, `build-proven.mjs`, `proven-assets.mjs` and `financial-comparison.mjs` are necessary consumers beyond the original draft’s shortened file list.

These are concrete LL04 contract decisions, not a new design program. Independent contract review can resolve them under existing authority before one writer changes behavior. Missing live accounting blocks dependent financial dispatch; it does not block this preparation or LL01 repair.

## Verification and limits

Only source inspection, interface extraction, source hashing and independent arithmetic construction were performed. No source implementation, test execution, compiler, K, proof, Docker, network, wallet/private-file access or accounting action ran. Contract/source approval remains pending. LL06 actual compilation, LL07 Docker results, LL08 finalized Preview effects, raw process exit and containment all retain their separate prerequisites; full correspondence and mandatory correctness remain required under SP09.

--- BEGIN FILE deliverables/language-to-ledger-2026-09-12/sprints/LL04/authority-design-proposal.md SHA256 5802a1f8e1c78d26f89a88ca6ef50820e85ea57d2500ce62d97b3abab148f9dc ---
# LL04 authority design proposal

**Status: proposed for independent Opus/Astra review.** No implementation, signature, compiler, wallet access or public action ran. This extends [the full ledger contract](ledger-contract-draft.md); every full state field, ordered effect, bound, obligation and historical acceptance limit remains required.

## Selected design

Use an explicit, one-time native maintenance transaction signed by the existing debtor wallet to activate the exact reviewed financial verifier keys. Deploy a fresh lifecycle instance with only deterministic `initialize` enabled. After its exact genesis is finalized, the debtor signs one update that enables `originate`, `accrue`, `repay` and `settle`, removes `initialize`, and replaces maintenance authority with an empty committee whose threshold is one. No financial circuit exists on the initial deployed instance, so possession of a role secret or a host consent flag cannot create debt before activation.

This uses installed ledger-v8 maintenance operations and the existing wallet `signData` callback. It introduces a real setup transaction; it is not an assertion that possession of a maintenance key means assent. The signature approves a precise deployment address and verifier-key update. The debtor signing consumer must show and verify the exact source, profile, roles, terms, cap, complete genesis and permission policy that those bytes authorize.

Origination is funded by the existing lender wallet; repayment and settlement by the existing borrower wallet. Accrual is explicitly permitted to any caller who satisfies the frozen source predicates, eligible time, next period, lifetime cap and work bounds. This permission is in the immutable descriptor approved by the debtor. It grants no spending authority over another wallet; the actual caller funds its own fee.

**Remaining limitation:** Compact `receiveUnshielded` does not name an input owner. The actual provider and independent native-input observer enforce lender/borrower funding identity. This proposal does not establish that an arbitrary alternative client is rejected by the ledger solely for using another payer. That predicate remains open; independent review must not convert this boundary into an unqualified ledger authorization or correspondence claim.

## Exact deployment and signature bindings

The proposed immutable descriptor includes every `wireAndLedgerBindings` field in the JSON. It binds Source5 primitive bytes and Core4/schema/action order; profile, registered bounds and canonicalization; lifecycle/kernel/lowering identities; full generated artifact commitments; exact native role addresses and public keys; Cash domain/issuer mapping; all principal, cap, conversion, allocation and accrual terms; complete financial genesis and ordinary genesis; and the explicit public-accrual policy. Persist the actual full state. A digest supplements the state and cannot replace it with a reduced projection.

For this source, the loan is Loan1, Borrower owes Lender principal100 with cap110, Cash denomination/asset, conversion1/scale0/none, AccrualFirst, rate1/10 floor, period60 and firstPeriodStart1000. Initial balances are Lender100, Borrower10, Other/Token7; allowances100/0,110/0,3/1; no obligations or used identities; work512/17/reserve16; phase0/paid0. Retain exact ordered arrays and numeric encodings. Dynamic source IDs/arguments remain dynamic; D1/O1/A1/P1/R1/P2/R2 are oracle inputs, not a new reduced source language.

Construct the generated genesis descriptor and native bootstrap state before deriving the new deployment address. Use only the `initialize` verifier and maintenance authority `[existingBorrowerUnshieldedVerifyingKey], threshold1, counter0`. The constructor/initialize pair must enforce the precise declared genesis, with initialize callable once and no arbitrary state setter or other operation/version present. Initialize records actual native funding/mint provenance for Lender100/Borrower10 and the unchanged Other row. Any required funding setup remains a real additional action; neither a host balance nor the old20-billion borrower mint suffices.

A new lifecycle preparation path can build a native `ContractState`, copy actual generated constructor `data` and legitimate native balances, install only the bootstrap `ContractOperation`, set the public-key authority, and then form `ContractDeploy`. Do not edit an existing prepared deployment or change its address after freezing it. The current `prepareFinancialDeployment` does not expose this behavior; its old private signing-key flow and deployed instances remain historical. No raw debtor secret is needed: use public key and signing callbacks.

After canonical finalized initialize readback, construct one native `MaintenanceUpdate(contractAddress, orderedUpdates, 0n)` with this exact order:

1. `VerifierKeyRemove("initialize", ContractOperationVersion("v3"))`.
2. `VerifierKeyInsert("originate", v3 exact reviewed originate key)`.
3. `VerifierKeyInsert("accrue", v3 exact reviewed accrue key)`.
4. `VerifierKeyInsert("repay", v3 exact reviewed repay key)`.
5. `VerifierKeyInsert("settle", v3 exact reviewed settle key)`.
6. `ReplaceAuthority(ContractMaintenanceAuthority([], 1, 1n))`.

The borrower consumer verifies all six updates, exact current operation map and full genesis, then calls the existing `unshieldedKeystore.signData(update.dataToSign)` and `update.addSignature(0n, signature)`. Verify against the expected borrower public key before forming `Transaction.fromParts(expectedNetworkId, undefined, undefined, Intent.new(admittedTTL).addMaintenanceUpdate(update))`. This describes use of installed interfaces, not executed code. Submit with the actual guarded provider and pinned SDK `submitTx`. Do not use several separately submitted maintenance helpers: an intermediate unfrozen key map would change the reviewed consent boundary.

Native `dataToSign` contains the maintenance domain, contract address, ordered updates and old counter. The address commits initial native state and nonce; it does not automatically commit arbitrary later state. Genesis/head binding therefore depends on exact immutable genesis committed by deployment and deterministic one-shot initialize. Each financial circuit must require initialized state; originate also requires the exact consented financial genesis/revision0, then each later action consumes the real next revision. A stored expected-head value supplied by a caller is insufficient.

Native maintenance can technically be submitted before initialize: it has no financial-head condition. The approved consumer signs only after finalized initialization. Even a prematurely relayed valid activation must be unable to create debt because all financial circuits assert initialization/genesis; removing initialize early may strand this new instance. Preserve that failure and charges instead of silently recreating it. This limitation is included in the controls.

The native signature has no separate network field. Bind network/genesis/protocol in the deployment descriptor and verified consumer chain context. Retain exact finalized initialize/activation transaction IDs, block references, native operation maps and authority counters in the existing observation flow. Do not invent a self-referential receipt hash inside its own signature or claim that a declaration of networkTag verifies the real chain. A mirrored-chain replay requires an actual native control before claiming cryptographic exclusion.

After activation, only the four exact financial verifier keys may remain, all unsupported operation versions absent, and authority must be empty/threshold1/counter1. Threshold0 would allow unauthorized updates. Financial data, phase, revision0, balances, allowances, work and all source identity histories are unchanged. The native ledger has a separate setup transition; keep it in native history. Do not insert consent into the seven source financial effects.

## Actual caller and funding

Use two existing wallet contexts with separately bound native public identities. The borrower context owns consent signing and borrower-funded repayment/settlement. The lender context owns origination funding. Each immutable provider retains its own payer/account/reservation identity; the current provider cannot switch accounts under one record. Explicitly allocate the lifecycle total across those records under existing accounting instead of resetting a consumed allocation. The selected bounded run may use borrower as the fee payer for deploy, initialize, activation and public accrue, but public-accrual permission is not borrower-only.

The actual source-derived originate calls receive100 Cash/send100 to Borrower with source Transfer/Origination checks; the provider must select and sign lender-owned native inputs, and independent readback must verify them. Repay and settle receive source-computed Cash and send to Lender, with borrower input signatures checked. Retain native input gross caps and change, complete effects and cumulative native DUST fees. A native signature proves authority to consume its own input; it does not by itself cause Compact to assert that its owner is the source Lender/Borrower. The JSON records this as an unresolved arbitrary-caller ledger predicate, not a source success claim.

The independent complete oracle remains the earlier contract: originate principal100/accrued0; accrue100/10; repay30 leaves80/0; settle80 leaves0/0 with settled obligation retained. Lifetime incurred remains110. Work and all ordered financial IDs/effects carry across each actual head without reset. Public permission for accrue cannot override source ensures or allow a second accrual/period.

## Required concrete consumer changes

- [generate.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/custody/generate.mjs): Source-derived lifecycle circuits; deterministic initialize; immutable descriptor/genesis and full state; financial actions require initialized and authenticated current revision. Publish bootstrap and exact financial operation maps separately.
- [prepare-deployment.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/prepare-deployment.mjs): New lifecycle preparation: construct fresh native state from real generated constructor data, only initialize operation, borrower public-key authority. Fix final state before ContractDeploy/address. Preserve old six-arg helper and recovery deployments.
- [integrate-local.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/integrate-local.mjs): Obtain two existing actor contexts by public-bound callbacks; verify exact borrower consent manifest/deployment/genesis before signData; construct one native six-update transaction and submit through guarded provider+SDK submitTx.
- [providers.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/providers.mjs): Separate payer-bound immutable provider/reservation identities per borrower/lender; verify exact maintenance action and updates in proposed consent path; preserve gross/fee limits and history. No context mutation under old allocation.
- [run-local.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/run-local.mjs): Actual seven-stage lifecycle caller. Lender pays originate; borrower pays setup/repay/settle; selected actual accrue caller pays fee. Extend closed stage diagnostics and completion predicate.
- [receipt.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/receipt.mjs): Decode and verify native MaintenanceUpdate independently; current ContractCall receipt path cannot represent consent. Retain full native before/after operation map, authority, data and balances; chain/head/finality and fee attribution.
- [financial-comparison.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/financial-comparison.mjs): Independent activation diff limited to key map/authority/counter; financial state exactly invariant. Real lender and borrower native inputs/outputs, full inherited source oracle and all setup fees.
- [build-proven.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/build-proven.mjs): Compile/pin bootstrap initialize and four real source-derived financial circuits only under later LL06 admission; compiled evidence is absent here.
- [proven-assets.mjs](/home/charl/Moriarty/experiments/moriarty-midnight-financial/ledger/proven-assets.mjs): Validate full reviewed artifact bundle, selective deployment operation map and exact activated operation map; do not require financial keys to be deployed before debtor signature.

No new generic authorization framework or registry is proposed. These are changes to the existing lifecycle generator, native deployment/call boundary and complete observer. Exact lowerer/full-state encoding remains the original LL04 contract decision; consent does not replace those obligations.

## Required resource and history delta

The proposed fresh-instance sequence is **deploy → initialize → activate consent → originate → accrue → repay → settle**, seven separate submissions when the six activation updates share one transaction. Any additional asset funding/setup increases this actual count. This is a design count, not an authorized allowance. It cannot fit the inherited closed four-call deploy/initialize/accrue/settle plan without an explicit reviewed amendment.

Record new setup identity, exact plan/schema/stage changes, all actor funding, gross limits, native fees, current deadline and remaining attempts in the existing resource/admission records through the user-required substantive decision process. Preserve the expired September11 window, consumed attempts, historical charges, old loan deployment and private stores. Do not reuse historical unused slack or claim current missing accounting exists. No numerical fee cap, new wallet or execution attempt is authorized by this proposal.

## Independent controls

All controls below are specified-only; no signature, native simulation or test was run.

- **LL04-AUTH-P01 (positive)** Exact bootstrap and initialized genesis, existing debtor signature on exact six-update activation, valid counter0 and finalized success. Only four exact financial verifier keys remain; maintenance committee empty threshold1 counter1; financial PRE, ordinary PRE, work and all histories unchanged. Full native setup and fee receipt retained.
- **LL04-AUTH-P02 (positive)** Authenticated consent state, real lender wallet funding100 through reviewed source originate with D1/O1. Native input owners/signatures match lender; borrower receives100; full prior oracle originate state/effects including retained terms/cap and work match.
- **LL04-AUTH-P03 (positive)** Unprivileged caller requests accrue A1/period1 with valid constrained T under explicit public-accrual policy. No borrower secret needed; exactly10 interest and65 work charged, no Cash transfer; complete cursor/history matches source. Policy permission is explicit in debtor-consented descriptor.
- **LL04-AUTH-P04 (positive)** Real borrower funds repay30 P1/R1 then settle80 P2/R2 at successive native heads. Complete full-state/effect oracle matches; distinct native signature/gross-input/fee evidence per call; consent genesis remains retained after obligation settles.
- **LL04-AUTH-N01 (negative)** Originate/accrue/repay/settle before activation or omit activation result. SDK missing operation/native contract verification rejects. A host consent=true or role secret cannot enable an absent key.
- **LL04-AUTH-N02 (negative)** Activation has no signature, maintenance/deployer key signature, lender-only signature, wrong committee index or duplicate signature index. Native authorization rejects; data, operations, authority and financial state remain unchanged. Failed fee debit is separately observed, never asserted zero.
- **LL04-AUTH-N03 (negative)** After signing, change address, one operation name, one verifier byte, update order, remove the freeze, or change counter. Exact native maintenance signature or replay checks reject; no partial enabling is accepted.
- **LL04-AUTH-N04 (negative)** Borrower signs while expecting cap110 but deployment commits120, wrong debtor/lender, source/profile/bounds/Core, conversion, allocation policy, time terms, initial liabilities, work or histories. Independent borrower pre-sign consumer rejects exact deployment/genesis/descriptor mismatch. Cryptographic signature cannot establish informed approval if signer blindly signs; this is an explicit signer obligation.
- **LL04-AUTH-N05 (negative)** Prepare update at financial revision1 or permit a mutable bootstrap circuit to change genesis before activation. Reject descriptor/readback and deployment. Selected design requires deterministic initialize once and no enabled financial/mutation circuit before activation; if not established, head binding is missing.
- **LL04-AUTH-N06 (negative)** Replay exact activation after success or attempt a new update under the old debtor key. Counter or impossible authority rejects; empty committee threshold0 is an invalid design substitution.
- **LL04-AUTH-N07 (negative)** Deploy with hidden operation/alternate version or leave initialize/extra verifier after activation. Exact operation-map readback rejects; checking only four expected names is insufficient.
- **LL04-AUTH-N08 (negative)** Relay maintenance signature to another network or mirrored deployment with matching declared tag. Consumer rejects live genesis/protocol/contract history mismatch. Standalone maintenance signature has no explicit network field; do not count this as an in-circuit rejection without a real native control.
- **LL04-AUTH-N09 (negative)** Originate using borrower/third-party Cash UTXOs but correct token/amount; repay using lender UTXOs. Reviewed provider rejects owner mismatch before signing and complete observer refuses financial acceptance. Direct arbitrary-client native transaction must separately test the documented payer-enforcement gap; do not claim native receive alone rejects it.
- **LL04-AUTH-N10 (negative)** Provide lender address or capability secret without a matching existing lender wallet/funded UTXOs. Fail funding preflight; no substitute wallet creation or fictional reserve. Borrower receives funds only after real matching transfer.
- **LL04-AUTH-N11 (negative)** Public accrual with old time, window mismatch, wrong period, duplicate ID, changed terms, cap overflow, extra Cash effect or suffix ensure failure. Source-derived circuit rejects atomically under actual full time context; public permission does not waive any financial constraint.
- **LL04-AUTH-N12 (negative)** Transfer100 from gross150 under cap100 and return50; add other asset/recipient or skip consent fee in cumulative charges. Gross/complete effect/cumulative fee checks reject; setup fees and historical charges remain visible.
- **LL04-AUTH-N13 (negative)** Report activation from signature verification, indexer-only status, partial segment, or expected JSON without native finality/readback. Remain incomplete; require signed native bytes, successful maintenance action and exact finalized state. A maintenance action is not observed as a ContractCall.
- **LL04-AUTH-N14 (negative)** Move consent into source action history, reset financial work after activation, delete Other Token row, or erase settled obligation/IDs. Full state/history comparison rejects. Setup lives in native history; four financial actions and seven ordered source effects retain original identities.
- **LL04-AUTH-N15 (negative)** Swap lender/borrower provider under one reservation file, restart spent allocation, or run new seven-stage sequence under old four-call plan. Identity/resource admission rejects; no accounting reset or expired AFK clock revival.
- **LL04-AUTH-N16 (negative)** Submit already signed maintenance activation before initialize. It may activate keys because maintenance itself has no financial-state condition. Each financial circuit must assert initialized plus exact consented genesis at originate; consumer requires initialize finalized before signing. Early activation cannot originate debt; it may strand the instance after initialize removal and must be reported as failed setup, not silently recovered.

## Disposition for review

The selected activation uses existing native public-key authorization and provides an explicit debtor act binding the exact frozen program. Role secrets, blind maintenance-key possession and bearer tokens were rejected as substitutes. Public bounded accrual is a deliberate permission choice to review, not an inference from the old borrower-secret accrue wrapper.

Review must address the payer-enforcement boundary, immutable-genesis/head assumption, early activation failure and chain replay boundary explicitly. The design does not close LL04.1/LL04.2, authenticate arbitrary lowerings, prove native/Compact correspondence, or waive mandatory SP09/PCD acceptance. LL06 compilation, LL07 Docker results and LL08 Preview settlement retain their original gates.

The JSON preserves the exact original requirement identities, full state inventory, source facts/preimages, interfaces, alternatives and controls. Only these two proposal deliverables were written.

--- BEGIN FILE .worktrees/r3-native/experiments/moriarty-midnight-network/hello-world/node_modules/@midnight-ntwrk/compact-runtime/dist/built-ins.d.ts SHA256 619be60985d945809f2b30b5297d429fac3bedafbf94920bf91e5470d97da6e9 ---
import * as ocrt from '@midnight-ntwrk/onchain-runtime-v3';
import { CompactType, JubjubPoint } from './compact-types.js';
/**
 * Field addition
 * returns the result of adding x and y, wrapping if necessary
 * x and y are assumed to be values in the range [0, FIELD_MODULUS)
 */
export declare function addField(x: bigint, y: bigint): bigint;
/**
 * Field subtraction
 * returns the result of subtracting y from x, wrapping if necessary
 * x and y are assumed to be values in the range [0, FIELD_MODULUS)
 */
export declare function subField(x: bigint, y: bigint): bigint;
/**
 * Field multiplication
 * returns the result of multipying x and y, wrapping if necessary
 * x and y are assumed to be values in the range [0, FIELD_MODULUS)
 */
export declare function mulField(x: bigint, y: bigint): bigint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `transientHash` function
 *
 * This function is a circuit-efficient compression function from arbitrary
 * data to field elements, which is not guaranteed to persist between upgrades.
 * It should not be used to derive state data, but can be used for consistency
 * checks.
 */
export declare function transientHash<A>(rtType: CompactType<A>, value: A): bigint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `transientCommit` function
 *
 * This function is a circuit-efficient commitment function from arbitrary
 * values representable in Compact, and a field element commitment opening, to
 * field elements, which is not guaranteed to persist between
 * upgrades. It should not be used to derive state data, but can be used for
 * consistency checks.
 *
 * @throws If `opening` is out of range for field elements
 */
export declare function transientCommit<A>(rtType: CompactType<A>, value: A, opening: bigint): bigint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `persistentHash` function
 *
 * This function is a non-circuit-optimised hash function for mostly arbitrary
 * data. It is guaranteed to persist between upgrades, with the exception of
 * devnet. It *should* be used to derive state data, and not for consistency
 * checks where avoidable.
 *
 * Note that data containing `Opaque` elements *may* throw runtime errors, and
 * cannot be relied upon as a consistent representation.
 *
 * @throws If `rtType` encodes a type containing Compact 'Opaque' types
 */
export declare function persistentHash<A>(rtType: CompactType<A>, value: A): Uint8Array;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `persistentCommit` function
 *
 * This function is a non-circuit-optimised commitment function from arbitrary
 * values representable in Compact, and a 256-bit bytestring opening, to a
 * 256-bit bytestring. It is guaranteed to persist between upgrades. It
 * *should* be used to derive state data, and not for consistency checks where
 * avoidable.
 *
 * Note that data containing `Opaque` elements *may* throw runtime errors, and
 * cannot be relied upon as a consistent representation.
 *
 * @throws If `rtType` encodes a type containing Compact 'Opaque' types, or
 * `opening` is not 32 bytes long
 */
export declare function persistentCommit<A>(rtType: CompactType<A>, value: A, opening: Uint8Array): Uint8Array;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `degradeToTransient` function
 *
 * This function "degrades" the output of a {@link persistentHash} or
 * {@link persistentCommit} to a field element, which can then be used in
 * {@link transientHash} or {@link transientCommit}.
 *
 * @throws If `x` is not 32 bytes long
 */
export declare function degradeToTransient(x: Uint8Array): bigint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `upgradeFromTransient` function
 *
 * This function "upgrades" the output of a {@link transientHash} or
 * {@link transientCommit} to 256-bit byte string, which can then be used in
 * {@link persistentHash} or {@link persistentCommit}.
 *
 * @throws If `x` is not a valid field element
 */
export declare function upgradeFromTransient(x: bigint): Uint8Array;
export declare function jubjubPointX(pt: JubjubPoint): bigint;
export declare function jubjubPointY(pt: JubjubPoint): bigint;
export declare function constructJubjubPoint(x: bigint, y: bigint): JubjubPoint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `hashToCurve` function
 *
 * This function maps arbitrary values representable in Compact to elliptic
 * curve points in the proof system's embedded curve.
 *
 * Outputs are guaranteed to have unknown discrete logarithm with respect to
 * the group base, and any other output, but are not guaranteed to be unique (a
 * given input can be proven correct for multiple outputs).
 *
 * Inputs of different types may have the same output, if they have the same
 * field-aligned binary representation.
 */
export declare function hashToCurve<A>(rtType: CompactType<A>, x: A): JubjubPoint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `ecAdd` function
 *
 * This function add two elliptic curve points (in multiplicative notation)
 */
export declare function ecAdd(a: JubjubPoint, b: JubjubPoint): JubjubPoint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `ecMul` function
 *
 * This function multiplies an elliptic curve point by a scalar (in
 * multiplicative notation)
 */
export declare function ecMul(a: JubjubPoint, b: bigint): JubjubPoint;
/**
 * The Compact builtin `ecMulGenerator` function
 *
 * This function multiplies the primary group generator of the embedded curve
 * by a scalar (in multiplicative notation)
 */
export declare function ecMulGenerator(b: bigint): JubjubPoint;
/**
 * Concatenates multiple {@link AlignedValue}s
 * @internal
 */
export declare function alignedConcat(...values: ocrt.AlignedValue[]): ocrt.AlignedValue;

export function runtimeCoinNullifier(coin: AlignedValue, sender_evidence: AlignedValue): AlignedValue;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the Merkle tree leaf hash primitive.
 * @internal
 */
export function leafHash(value: AlignedValue): AlignedValue;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the max aligned size primitive.
 * @internal
 */
export function maxAlignedSize(alignment: Alignment): bigint;

/**
 * Returns the maximum representable value in the proof systems scalar field
 * (that is, 1 less than the prime modulus)
 */
export function maxField(): bigint;

/**
 * Converts input, output, and transcript information into a proof preimage
 * suitable to pass to a `ProvingProvider`.
 *
 * The `key_location` parameter is a string used to identify the circuit by
 * proving machinery, for backwards-compatibility, if unset it defaults to
 * `'dummy'`.
 */
export function proofDataIntoSerializedPreimage(
  input: AlignedValue,
  output: AlignedValue,
  public_transcript: Op<AlignedValue>[],
  private_transcript_outputs: AlignedValue[],
  key_location?: string,
): Uint8Array;

/**
 * Takes a bigint modulus the proof systems scalar field
 */
export function bigIntModFr(x: bigint): bigint;

/**
 * Internal conversion between field-aligned binary values and bigints within
 * the scalar field
 * @internal
 * @throws If the value does not encode a field element
 */
export function valueToBigInt(x: Value): bigint;

/**
 * Internal conversion between bigints and their field-aligned binary
 * representation
 * @internal
 */
export function bigIntToValue(x: bigint): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the transient hash primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link val} does not have alignment {@link align}
 */
export function transientHash(align: Alignment, val: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the transient commitment primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link val} does not have alignment {@link align}, or
 * {@link opening} does not encode a field element
 */
export function transientCommit(align: Alignment, val: Value, opening: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the persistent hash primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link val} does not have alignment {@link align}, or any
 * component has a compress alignment
 */
export function persistentHash(align: Alignment, val: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the persistent commitment primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link val} does not have alignment {@link align},
 * {@link opening} does not encode a 32-byte bytestring, or any component has a
 * compress alignment
 */
export function persistentCommit(align: Alignment, val: Value, opening: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the degrade to transient primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link persistent} does not encode a 32-byte bytestring
 */
export function degradeToTransient(persistent: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the upgrade from transient primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link transient} does not encode a field element
 */
export function upgradeFromTransient(transient: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the hash to curve primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link val} does not have alignment {@link align}
 */
export function hashToCurve(align: Alignment, val: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the elliptic curve addition primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If either input does not encode an elliptic curve point
 */
export function ecAdd(a: Value, b: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the elliptic curve multiplication primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws If {@link a} does not encode an elliptic curve point or {@link b}
 * does not encode a field element
 */
export function ecMul(a: Value, b: Value): Value;

/**
 * Internal implementation of the elliptic curve generator multiplication
 * primitive
 * @internal
 * @throws if {@link val} does not encode a field element
 */
export function ecMulGenerator(val: Value): Value;

/**
 * Runs a VM program against an initial stack, with an optional gas limit
 */
export function runProgram(initial: VmStack, ops: Op<null>[], cost_model: CostModel, gas_limit?: RunningCost): VmResults;

/**
 * An individual operation, or entry point of a contract, consisting primarily
 * of a ZK verifier keys, potentially for different versions of the proving
 * system.
 *
 * Only the latest available version is exposed to this API.
 *
 * Note that the serialized form of the key is checked on initialization
 */
export class ContractOperation {
  constructor();

  verifierKey: Uint8Array;

  serialize(): Uint8Array;

  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): ContractOperation;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

/**
 * A committee permitted to make changes to this contract. If a threshold of
 * the public keys in this committee sign off, they can change the rules of
 * this contract, or recompile it for a new version.
 *
 * If the threshold is greater than the number of committee members, it is
 * impossible for them to sign anything.
 */
export class ContractMaintenanceAuthority {
  /**
   * Constructs a new authority from its components
   *
   * If not supplied, `counter` will default to `0n`. Values should be
   * non-negative, and at most 2^32 - 1.
   *
   * At deployment, `counter` must be `0n`, and any subsequent update should
   * set counter to exactly one greater than the current value.
   */
  constructor(committee: Array<SignatureVerifyingKey>, threshold: number, counter?: bigint);

  /**
   * The committee public keys
   */
  readonly committee: Array<SignatureVerifyingKey>;
  /**
   * How many keys must sign rule changes
   */
  readonly threshold: number;
  /**
   * The replay protection counter
   */
  readonly counter: bigint;

  serialize(): Uint8Array;

  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): ContractState;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

/**
 * The state of a contract, consisting primarily of the {@link data} accessible
 * directly to the contract, and the map of {@link ContractOperation}s that can
 * be called on it, the keys of which can be accessed with {@link operations},
 * and the individual operations can be read with {@link operation} and written
 * to with {@link setOperation}.
 */
export class ContractState {
  /**
   * Creates a blank contract state
   */
  constructor();

  /**
   * Return a list of the entry points currently registered on this contract
   */
  operations(): Array<string | Uint8Array>

  /**
   * Get the operation at a specific entry point name
   */
  operation(operation: string | Uint8Array): ContractOperation | undefined;

  /**
   * Set a specific entry point name to contain a given operation
   */
  setOperation(operation: string | Uint8Array, value: ContractOperation): void;

  /**
   * Runs a series of operations against the current state, and returns the
   * results
   */
  query(query: Op<null>[], cost_model: CostModel): GatherResult[];

  serialize(): Uint8Array;

  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): ContractState;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  /**
   * The current value of the primary state of the contract
   */
  data: ChargedState;
  /**
   * The maintenance authority associated with this contract
   */
  maintenanceAuthority: ContractMaintenanceAuthority;
  /**
   * The public balances held by this contract
   */
  balance: Map<TokenType, bigint>;
}

/**
 * Provides the information needed to fully process a transaction, including
 * information about the rest of the transaction, and the state of the chain at
 * the time of execution.
 */
export class QueryContext {
  /**
   * Construct a basic context from a contract's address and current state
   * value
   */
  constructor(state: ChargedState, address: ContractAddress);

  /**
   * Register a given coin commitment as being accessible at a specific index,
   * for use when receiving coins in-contract, and needing to record their
   * index to later spend them
   */
  insertCommitment(comm: CoinCommitment, index: bigint): QueryContext;

  /**
   * Internal counterpart to {@link insertCommitment}; upgrades an encoded
   * {@link ShieldedCoinInfo} to an encoded {@link QualifiedShieldedCoinInfo} using the
   * inserted commitments
   * @internal
   */
  qualify(coin: Value): Value | undefined;

  /**
   * Runs a transcript in verifying mode against the current query context,
   * outputting a new query context, with the {@link state} and {@link effects}
   * from after the execution.
   */
  runTranscript(transcript: Transcript<AlignedValue>, cost_model: CostModel): QueryContext;

  /**
   * Runs a sequence of operations in gather mode, returning the results of the
   * gather.
   */
  query(ops: Op<null>[], cost_model: CostModel, gas_limit?: RunningCost): QueryResults;

  /**
   * Converts the QueryContext to {@link VmStack}.
   */
  toVmStack(): VmStack;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  /**
   * The address of the contract
   */
  readonly address: ContractAddress;
  /**
   * The block-level information accessible to the contract
   */
  block: CallContext;
  /**
   * The commitment indices map accessible to the contract, primarily via
   * {@link qualify}
   */
  readonly comIndices: Map<CoinCommitment, bigint>;
  /**
   * The effects that occurred during execution against this context, should
   * match those declared in a {@link Transcript}
   */
  effects: Effects;
  /**
   * The current contract state retained in the context
   */
  readonly state: ChargedState;
}

/**
 * A cost model for calculating transaction fees
 */
export class CostModel {
  private constructor();

  /**
   * The initial cost model of Midnight
   */
  static initialCostModel(): CostModel;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

/**
 * The results of making a query against a specific state or context
 */
export class QueryResults {
  private constructor();

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  /**
   * The context state after executing the query. This can be used to execute
   * further queries
   */
  readonly context: QueryContext;
  /**
   * Any events/results that occurred during or from the query
   */
  readonly events: GatherResult[];
  /**
   * The measured cost of executing the query
   */
  readonly gasCost: RunningCost;
}

/**
 * Represents a fixed-depth Merkle tree storing hashed data, whose preimages
 * are unknown
 */
export class StateBoundedMerkleTree {
  /**
   * Create a blank tree with the given height
   */
  constructor(height: number);

  /**
   * Internal implementation of the merkle tree root primitive.
   * Returns undefined if the tree has not been fully hashed.
   * @internal
   */
  root(): AlignedValue | undefined;

  /**
   * Internal implementation of the finding path primitive.
   * Returns undefined if the leaf is not in the tree.
   * @internal
   */
  findPathForLeaf(
    leaf: AlignedValue,
    indexStart?: bigint,
    indexEnd?: bigint,
    alreadyHashed?: boolean,
  ): AlignedValue | undefined;

  /**
   * Internal implementation of the path construction primitive
   * @internal
   * @throws If the index is out-of-bounds for the tree
   */
  pathForLeaf(index: bigint, leaf: AlignedValue): AlignedValue;

  /**
   * Inserts a value into the Merkle tree, returning the updated tree
   * @throws If the index is out-of-bounds for the tree
   */
  update(index: bigint, leaf: AlignedValue): StateBoundedMerkleTree;

  /**
   * Rehashes the tree, updating all internal hashes and ensuring all
   * node hashes are present. Necessary because the onchain runtime does
   * not automatically rehash trees.
   */
  rehash(): StateBoundedMerkleTree;

  /**
   * Erases all but necessary hashes between, and inclusive of, `start` and
   * `end` inidices @internal
   * @throws If the indices are out-of-bounds for the tree, or `end < start`
   */
  collapse(start: bigint, end: bigint): StateBoundedMerkleTree;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  readonly height: number;
}

/**
 * Represents a key-value map, where keys are {@link AlignedValue}s, and values
 * are {@link StateValue}s.
 */
export class StateMap {
  constructor();

  keys(): AlignedValue[];

  get(key: AlignedValue): StateValue | undefined;

  insert(key: AlignedValue, value: StateValue): StateMap;

  remove(key: AlignedValue): StateMap;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

/**
 * Represents a {@link StateValue} with storage annotations.
 *
 * These track the state usage that has been charged for so far.
 */
export class ChargedState {
  constructor(state: StateValue);
  readonly state: StateValue;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

/**
 * Represents the core of a contract's state, and recursively represents each
 * of its components.
 *
 * There are different *classes* of state values:
 * - `null`
 * - Cells of {@link AlignedValue}s
 * - Maps from {@link AlignedValue}s to state values
 * - Bounded Merkle trees containing {@link AlignedValue} leaves
 * - Short (\<= 15 element) arrays of state values
 *
 * State values are *immutable*, any operations that mutate states will return
 * a new state instead.
 */
export class StateValue {
  private constructor();

  type(): 'null' | 'cell' | 'map' | 'array' | 'boundedMerkleTree';

  static newNull(): StateValue;

  static newCell(value: AlignedValue): StateValue;

  static newMap(map: StateMap): StateValue;

  static newBoundedMerkleTree(tree: StateBoundedMerkleTree): StateValue;

  static newArray(): StateValue;

  arrayPush(value: StateValue): StateValue;

  asCell(): AlignedValue;

  asMap(): StateMap | undefined;

  asBoundedMerkleTree(): StateBoundedMerkleTree | undefined;

  asArray(): StateValue[] | undefined;

  logSize(): number;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  /**
   * @internal
   */
  encode(): EncodedStateValue;

  /**
   * @internal
   */
  static decode(value: EncodedStateValue): StateValue;
}

/**
 * Represents the results of a VM call
 */
export class VmResults {
  private constructor();

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;

  /**
   * The events that got emitted by this VM invocation
   */
  readonly events: GatherResult[];
  /**
   * The computed gas cost of running this VM invocation
   */
  readonly gasCost: RunningCost;
  /**
   * The VM stack at the end of the VM invocation
   */
  readonly stack: VmStack;
}

/**
 * Represents the state of the VM's stack at a specific point. The stack is an
 * array of {@link StateValue}s, each of which is also annotated with whether
 * it is "strong" or "weak"; that is, whether it is permitted to be stored
 * on-chain or not.
 */
export class VmStack {
  constructor();

  push(value: StateValue, is_strong: boolean): void;

  removeLast(): void;

  length(): number;

  get(idx: number): StateValue | undefined;

  isStrong(idx: number): boolean | undefined;

  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}


/**
 * A zero-knowledge proof.
 */
export class Proof {
  constructor(data: String);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): Proof;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'proof';
  private type_: 'proof';
}

/**
 * The preimage, or data required to produce, a {@link Proof}.
 */
export class PreProof {
  constructor(data: String);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): PreProof;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'pre-proof';
  private type_: 'pre-proof';
}

/**
 * A unit type used to indicate the absence of proofs.
 */
export class NoProof {
  constructor();
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'no-proof';
  private type_: 'no-proof';
}

/**
 * How proofs are currently being represented, between:
 * - Actual zero-knowledge proofs, as should be transmitted to the network
 * - The data required to *produce* proofs, for constructing and preparing
 *   transactions.
 * - Proofs not being provided, largely for testing use or replaying already
 *   validated transactions.
 */
export type Proofish = Proof | PreProof | NoProof;

/**
 * A Fiat-Shamir proof of exponent binding (or ephemerally signing) an
 * {@link Intent}.
 */
export class Binding {
  constructor(data: String);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): Binding;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'binding';
  private type_: 'binding';
}

/**
 * Information that will be used to bind an {@link Intent} in the future, but
 * does not yet prevent modification of it.
 */
export class PreBinding {
  constructor(data: String);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): PreBinding;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'pre-binding';
  private type_: 'pre-binding';
}

export class NoBinding {
  constructor(data: String);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): NoBinding;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  instance: 'no-binding';
  private type_: 'no-binding';
}

/**
 * Whether an intent has binding cryptography applied or not. An intent's
 * content can no longer be modified after it is {@link Binding}.
 */
export type Bindingish = Binding | PreBinding | NoBinding;

export class SignatureEnabled {
  constructor(data: Signature);
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): SignatureEnabled;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  readonly instance: 'signature';
  private type_: 'signature';
}

export class SignatureErased {
  constructor();
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  readonly instance: 'signature-erased';
  private type_: 'signature-erased';
}

export type Signaturish = SignatureEnabled | SignatureErased;

/**
 * A type representing a transaction that has not been proven yet
 */
export type UnprovenInput = ZswapInput<PreProof>;

/**
 * A type representing a transaction output that has not been proven yet.
 */
export type UnprovenOutput = ZswapOutput<PreProof>;

/**
 * A type representing a transaction transient that has not been proven yet.
 */
export type UnprovenTransient = ZswapTransient<PreProof>;

/**
 * A type representing an offer that has not been proven yet.
 */
export type UnprovenOffer = ZswapOffer<PreProof>;

/**
 * A type representing an intent that has not been proven yet.
 */
export type UnprovenIntent = Intent<SignatureEnabled, PreProof, PreBinding>;

/**
 * An interactions with a contract
 */
export type ContractAction<P extends Proofish> = ContractCall<P> | ContractDeploy | MaintenanceUpdate;

/**
 * Strictness criteria for evaluating transaction well-formedness, used for
 * disabling parts of transaction validation for testing.
 */
export class WellFormedStrictness {
  constructor();

  /**
   * Whether to require the transaction to have a non-negative balance
   */
  enforceBalancing: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether to validate Midnight-native (non-contract) proofs in the transaction
   */
  verifyNativeProofs: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether to validate contract proofs in the transaction
   */
  verifyContractProofs: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether to enforce the transaction byte limit
   */
  enforceLimits: boolean;
  /**
   * Whether to enforce the signature verification
   */
  verifySignatures: boolean;
}

/**
 * Contains the raw file contents required for proving

export type ProvingKeyMaterial = {
  proverKey: Uint8Array,
  verifierKey: Uint8Array,
  ir: Uint8Array,
};

/**
 * A modelled cost of a transaction or block.
 */
export type SyntheticCost = {
  /**
   * The amount of (modelled) time spent reading from disk, measured in picoseconds.
   */
  readTime: bigint,
  /**
   * The amount of (modelled) time spent in single-threaded compute, measured in picoseconds.
   */
  computeTime: bigint,
  /**
   * The number of bytes of blockspace used
   */
  blockUsage: bigint,
  /**
   * The net number of (modelled) bytes written, i.e. max(0, absolute written bytes less deleted bytes).
   */
  bytesWritten: bigint,
  /**
   * The number of (modelled) bytes written temporarily or overwritten.
   */
  bytesChurned: bigint,
};

/**
 * A normalized form of {@link SyntheticCost}.
 */
export type NormalizedCost = {
  /**
   * The amount of (modelled) time spent reading from disk, measured in picoseconds.
   */
  readTime: number,
  /**
   * The amount of (modelled) time spent in single-threaded compute, measured in picoseconds.
   */
  computeTime: number,
  /**
   * The number of bytes of blockspace used
   */
  blockUsage: number,
  /**
   * The net number of (modelled) bytes written, i.e. max(0, absolute written bytes less deleted bytes).
   */
  bytesWritten: number,
  /**
   * The number of (modelled) bytes written temporarily or overwritten.
   */
  bytesChurned: number,
};

/**
 * An event emitted by the ledger
 */
export class Event {
  private constructor();
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): Event;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  readonly source: EventSource;
  readonly content: EventDetails;
}

/**
 * Where an event originated from
 */
export type EventSource = {
  /**
   * The hash of the originating transaction.
   */
  transactionHash: TransactionHash,
  /**
   * The logical event segment, that is, during which segment's execution the
   * event was emitted.
   */
  logicalSegment: number,
  /**
   * The physical event segment, that is, the segment of the transaction this
   * event's trigger is contained in.
   */
  physicalSegment: number,
};

/**
 * Details of the event emitted
 */
export type EventDetails =
  {
    tag: 'zswapInput',
    nullifier: Nullifier,
    contract: ContractAddress | undefined,
  } | {
    tag: 'zswapOutput',
    commitment: CoinCommitment,
    contract: ContractAddress | undefined,
    mtIndex: bigint,
  } | {
    tag: 'dustInitialUtxo',
    generation: DustGenerationInfo,
    generationIndex: bigint,
    blockTime: Date,
  } | {
    tag: 'dustGenerationDtimeUpdate',
    update: TreeInsertionPath<DustGenerationInfo>,
    blockTime: Date,
  } | {
    tag: 'dustSpendProcessed',
    commitment: DustCommitment,
    commitmentIndex: bigint,
    nullifier: DustNullifier,
    vFee: bigint,
    declaredTime: Date,
    blockTime: Date,
  } |
  // Other variants may be added and some events are not yet supported in this API.
  { tag: string };

/**
 * A path evidencing how to insert an entry into a Merkle tree, even if it is
 * collapsed.
 */
export type TreeInsertionPath<A> = {
  leafHash: string,
  annotation: A,
  path: TreeInsertionPathEntry[],
};

/**
 * A single entry in a {@link TreeInsertionPath}.
 */
export type TreeInsertionPathEntry = {
  hash: bigint | undefined,
  goesLeft: boolean,
};

/**
 * A secret key for the Dust, used to derive Dust UTxO nonces and prove credentials to spend Dust UTxOs
 */
export class DustSecretKey {
  private constructor();

  /**
   * Temporary method to create an instance of {@link DustSecretKey} from a bigint (its natural representation)
   * @param bigint
   */
  static fromBigint(bigint: bigint): DustSecretKey;

  /**
   * Create an instance of {@link DustSecretKey} from a seed.
   * @param seed
   */
  static fromSeed(seed: Uint8Array): DustSecretKey;

  publicKey: DustPublicKey;

  /**
   * Clears the dust secret key, so that it is no longer usable nor held in memory
   */
  clear(): void;
}

  static newFromCommitmentTree(state: DustUtxoState, start: bigint, end: bigint): DustStateMerkleTreeCollapsedUpdate;
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): DustStateMerkleTreeCollapsedUpdate;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
}

  constructor();
  serialize(): Uint8Array;
  static deserialize(raw: Uint8Array): DustState;
  toString(compact?: boolean): string;
  readonly utxo: DustUtxoState;
  readonly generation: DustGenerationState;
}
